meta.name: Administration Workspace
meta.description: Capability-oriented administration workspace for accounts, permissions, configuration, integrations, and sensitive system actions.

purpose: Allow authorized users to understand and change system configuration safely while separating ordinary settings, sensitive permissions, irreversible actions, and technical diagnostics.
useWhen: The user configures organization, account, user, role, integration, or product settings.
Actions have broad impact or elevated permission requirements.
The interface includes read-only status, editable configuration, and sensitive actions.
Administrative information must be grouped by capability rather than backend modules.
doNotUseWhen: The task is an ordinary operational workflow.
The screen is only a simple user profile form.
The dominant task is reviewing one record.
Technical diagnostics are being presented to ordinary users.

selectionQuestions: Which administrative capabilities belong to this workspace?
Which actions affect one user, one organization, or the complete system?
Which settings require immediate save, explicit save, or separate approval?
Which technical details are appropriate for the target role?
Which actions are destructive, reversible, or auditable?
How are permissions represented without relying on role-name comparisons?
Which configuration changes require reauthentication or elevated confirmation?

regions.name: Administration Header
regions.role: Identify the administrative scope, current organization context, and limited workspace-level actions.
prohibitedComponents: Raw tenant UUID as the primary identity

compact.layout: Stack title, organization context, and low-frequency overflow action.
compact.notes: Do not present sensitive actions here.

wide.layout: Horizontal header with context and utility overflow.

ultrawide.notes: Do not add technical metadata merely to fill space.

rules: The current administrative scope is explicit.
Production, staging, or environment context is visible only when operationally relevant.
Technical IDs remain secondary or copyable details.

regions.name: Administration Navigation
regions.role: Group administrative capabilities into predictable user-oriented categories.

sticky.compactBehavior: Transform into grouped select or disclosure navigation.

regions.visibilityCondition: Always visible when more than one administrative capability exists.

compact.layout: Grouped select or compact disclosure navigation.

medium.notes: Low-frequency areas may move to overflow.

wide.placement: Left administrative rail or grouped navigation above content.
wide.notes: Navigation remains separate from the global application navigation.

rules: Categories represent administrative jobs.
Users see only capabilities allowed by disclosure policy.
Security, integrations, billing, users, and general settings are not mixed without grouping.
Active state does not depend only on color.

regions.name: Administrative Scope Summary
regions.role: Present the identity, status, ownership, and risk context of the object being administered.
regions.visibilityCondition: Visible when an organization, account, integration, user, or role context must remain clear.

medium.layout: Two-column definition summary when content permits.

wide.notes: Do not create a large hero card.

rules: The summary clarifies what is being administered.
Status labels use user-facing terminology.
Sensitive values remain masked.
Technical identifiers appear only when they support an administrative task.

regions.name: Administration Content
regions.role: Host the active administrative capability using approved list, detail, or form patterns.
prohibitedComponents: All settings in one undifferentiated form

compact.notes: Nested tables use controlled overflow or approved list adaptation.

wide.layout: Primary administrative content with optional contextual information.

ultrawide.layout: Primary administrative content with constrained reading and form widths.

rules: Each capability has a clear heading and purpose.
Lists, forms, and detail areas use their corresponding nested recipes.
Permission configuration uses capability-oriented language.
Read-only and editable states remain explicit.

regions.name: Sensitive and Destructive Actions
regions.role: Isolate actions that disable, delete, revoke, reset, rotate, or materially alter administrative access.
prohibitedComponents: Secret value rendered in plain text
regions.visibilityCondition: Visible only to eligible capabilities and only when sensitive actions exist.

wide.notes: Do not place beside ordinary save actions.

rules: Sensitive actions appear after ordinary configuration.
Impact, scope, reversibility, and audit consequence are explicit.
Reauthentication is required when the approved security policy demands it.
Confirmation labels name the affected object.

regions.name: Audit and Diagnostics
regions.role: Provide authorized administrative history and technical diagnostics through controlled progressive disclosure.
regions.visibilityCondition: Visible only for authorized administrative or support roles.

compact.notes: Long identifiers wrap or copy safely.

wide.notes: Do not mix with ordinary settings.

rules: Audit history remains available when required.
Diagnostics expose only safe operational information.
Correlation identifiers may be copied.
Raw implementation details remain in logs rather than ordinary UI.

composition.columnPolicy: Compact navigation above content on narrow layouts and a constrained administration rail beside one primary content column on wide layouts.
spacingOwnership: The recipe owns spacing between header, administration navigation, scope summary, active content, sensitive actions, and diagnostics.
Nested list, form, and detail recipes own internal spacing.
DangerZone owns spacing between impact description and destructive controls.
surfacePolicy: Ordinary administrative content uses approved surfaces based on nested recipe needs.
Sensitive actions use a distinct semantic danger surface.
Diagnostics use a subdued or progressively disclosed surface.
Do not render every setting inside an unrelated white card on a dark canvas.
rules: Administration is grouped by capability.
Sensitive actions remain separated.
Technical diagnostics remain authorized and progressively disclosed.
Nested workflows reuse approved recipes.
prohibited: Mixing ordinary save and destructive actions.
Administration navigation based directly on backend modules.
Raw tokens, hashes, JWTs, or security implementation details.
Several independent light and dark theme conventions.
Role-name comparisons scattered through presentation code.

actions.primaryPlacement: Inside the active administrative capability or nested form recipe.
actions.secondaryPlacement: Section toolbars, administrative overflow, or contextual controls.
actions.destructivePlacement: Dedicated sensitive-actions region after ordinary configuration.
actions.bulkPlacement: Inside an approved administrative list workflow with explicit selection.
actions.overflowPolicy: Low-frequency export, diagnostic, and utility actions move to overflow.
actions.compactBehavior: Preserve the active capability's primary action and move utilities to overflow.
rules: The workspace header normally contains no dominant configuration action.
Each nested capability owns its save or create action.
Destructive actions never visually match ordinary configuration actions.

content.headingPolicy: One h1 identifies administration; each capability uses h2; nested sections use h3.
content.longContentPolicy: Organization names, capability labels, permission descriptions, and audit entries support realistic lengths.
content.truncationPolicy: Critical scope and permission information remains accessible in full; secondary technical identifiers may truncate with copy access.
content.emptyStatePlacement: Capability-specific empty states remain inside the active administration content and preserve navigation context.
content.loadingStrategy: Preserve administration navigation while loading the active capability; use local skeletons or loading states.
content.errorScope: Capability failures remain local when administration navigation and scope remain valid; authentication and tenant failures affect the route.
rules: Administrative labels are understandable to the target role.
Unknown configuration values are not silently presented as disabled.
Secret and sensitive values remain masked.
Technical errors are normalized.

responsive.minimumViewport: 320 CSS pixels with compact grouped administration navigation.
responsive.zoomExpectation: Administration must remain usable at 125% browser zoom.
responsive.internalOverflowPolicy: Permission matrices and tables may use approved internal overflow; forms and ordinary settings must stack.

transformations.change: Keep the administration rail constrained and preserve the active content width.
transformations.reason: Navigation should not consume additional space without informational benefit.

transformations.change: Move the administration rail above content or reduce it to compact navigation.
transformations.reason: The active configuration workflow requires sufficient content width.

transformations.change: Transform administrative navigation into a grouped select or disclosure, stack all configuration sections, and move utilities to overflow.
transformations.reason: Compact viewports cannot sustain a permanent secondary navigation rail and complex settings simultaneously.

states.rendering: Render administrative navigation and scope-shaped skeletons while capability and organization context load.
Render approved administrative capabilities, configuration, permissions, and eligible actions.
Explain missing users, integrations, roles, or configuration and provide an eligible next action.
Display non-blocking configuration risk, pending deprecation, or incomplete setup.
states.userAction: Review and correct or continue according to policy.

states.rendering: Render capability-local recovery without exposing technical response bodies.
Hide or block restricted administrative capability according to disclosure policy.
Keep available capabilities usable while isolating unavailable integrations or settings.
states.userAction: Continue or retry the affected capability.

states.rendering: Warn when configuration changed elsewhere and current editing context may be outdated.
Show progress for invitations, integration checks, permission updates, key rotation, or configuration mutations.
states.userAction: Wait or cancel only when supported.

landmarkMap: Administration navigation uses a labeled nav landmark.
Active administrative capability uses a labeled section.
Sensitive actions use a clearly labeled section.
Audit and diagnostics use a separate labeled section.
headingStructure: One h1 identifies the administration workspace.
Configuration groups, danger zones, and diagnostic groups use h3 when nested.
keyboard: Confirmation and reauthentication dialogs trap and restore focus.
announcements: Permission and configuration mutation outcomes are perceivable.
Sensitive-action pending and completion states are announced.
accessibility.colorIndependence: Permission state, environment, warning, danger, and disabled state do not depend only on color.
rules: Restricted controls are hidden, disabled with explanation, or read-only according to approved policy.
Danger zones must not rely solely on red borders.
Technical identifiers require meaningful labels.

prohibitedPatterns: Destructive actions styled as ordinary primary actions.
Permission checks based only on visible role names.
Every setting placed in one large undifferentiated form.
Technical HTTP messages shown to ordinary administrators.
dataMagnitude: Administrative lists may contain many users, roles, integrations, or audit events.
Organization names and integration labels may exceed fixture lengths.
performance: Load administrative capabilities independently when useful.
Do not fetch every administration module before the active category is known.
Invalidate only affected configuration and permission queries.
Clear context-dependent cache after organization switching.
implementation: Capability-based permission helpers control visibility and behavior.
Nested forms use the form-workflow recipe.
Nested collections use the searchable-list recipe.
Technical diagnostics are normalized through the approved error and telemetry layers.
Machine presence conditions come from presenceDefaults; visibilityCondition prose is explanatory only.

presenceDefaults.rationale: Administration always requires explicit workspace and organization scope orientation.
A workspace with only one available administrative capability must not render secondary navigation with no real choice.
Scope summary appears only when a concrete organization, account, integration, user, or role context must remain explicit.
The active administrative capability is the primary content of the workspace.
Sensitive actions appear only when such actions exist and the current capability is eligible to perform them.
Audit and diagnostics remain absent unless safe operational context exists and disclosure is authorized.

checks.description: The administration recipe must validate against the layout recipe schema.
checks.remediation: Correct invalid or missing recipe fields.

checks.description: Ordinary configuration, permissions, destructive actions, and diagnostics must remain structurally distinct.
checks.remediation: Regroup administrative capabilities and isolate sensitive regions.

checks.description: Missing capabilities must produce the approved hidden, disabled, read-only, or forbidden behavior.
checks.remediation: Correct capability evaluation and disclosure policy.

checks.description: Administration navigation, forms, matrices, and danger zones must not create page-level horizontal overflow.
checks.remediation: Correct responsive navigation, nested recipe behavior, or internal overflow.

checks.description: Secrets, raw tokens, hashes, and unsafe technical values must not appear in the interface.
checks.remediation: Remove, mask, or replace the value with a safe administrative representation.

checks.description: Administration navigation and privileged optional regions must follow typed capability and permission presence semantics.
checks.remediation: Correct craftDefaults/presenceDefaults and keep conditional regions required=false with cardinality.minimum=0.
